clue.text: Election hopes may split on this rock ?

definitions.text: Election hopes may split on this
definitions.meaning: a preliminary vote where party hopefuls are divided before the main contest
in old geology the first, oldest rocks were called by this term

explanation.surface: Someone warns that an election campaign may founder on a rocky obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A US-style preliminary election picks candidates, and geologists once classed the earliest rock strata as primary.

clue.text: Whereby gatekeeper walking round cupola records distance

definitions.text: Whereby gatekeeper walking round cupola records distance

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: St Peter keeps the gates of heaven
a dome is a cupola

explanation.surface: Heaven's gatekeeper strolls round a dome, logging how far he has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' signals the container. Read whole, the clue also describes the device: one by which someone walking records distance covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts steps and so measures how far someone has walked.

clue.text: I am getting machinery to put in

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
plant means industrial machinery

explanation.surface: Someone announces they are acquiring equipment to install.
explanation.definitionFit: To implant is to insert or embed something.

clue.text: Cheered an unusual devotion

indicators.note: unusual suggests the letters appear in an unusual arrangement

explanation.surface: Fans cheered a remarkable display of loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges CHEERED AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Adherence is steady attachment or loyalty to a cause.

clue.text: Small boat lay up around the point

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one piece wraps the other
in a down clue up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
W, west, is a compass point

explanation.surface: A small boat is laid up near the headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LAY into YAL in this down clue, and 'around' puts it around W.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawl is a small two-masted sailing vessel.

clue.text: Burglar held by fund-raisers

definitions.meaning: A. J. ... is the gentleman cracksman of E. W. Hornung's stories
lotteries for prizes are staged by charities to collect money

explanation.surface: A thief is being harboured by a group of charity collectors.
explanation.definitionFit: Hornung's fictional gentleman thief bears this surname, and charity lotteries with tickets drawn for prizes go by the same word.

clue.text: No use inviting them not to stand on ceremony

definitions.text: No use inviting them not to stand on ceremony

parts.words: No use inviting them not to stand on ceremony
parts.note: people devoted to formal rites cannot be talked into informality

explanation.definitionFit: Ritualists insist on rite and formality, so asking them to be informal is futile.

clue.text: Smith-where or how he can make money ?

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workplace, or how he might mint money.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a smithy, and to forge money is to counterfeit it.

clue.text: Tract on Eve's mini-skirt?

definitions.meaning: Eve covered herself with a fig leaf, so a small one is her short skirt

explanation.surface: A pamphlet about Eve's short skirt.
explanation.walkthrough: A small leaf is a leaflet, and Eve's skirt in Genesis was made of fig leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaflet is a printed handout, and a small leaf would serve as Eve's tiny garment.

clue.text: Bill finds US president on board

indicators.note: on board means inside a ship, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: SS, steamship, stands for a vessel boarded
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Bill discovers an American president aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill Sikes is the brutal burglar in Dickens's Oliver Twist; 'on board' means inside SS, a steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill Sikes is the villain in Dickens's novel, so the first name points to him.

clue.text: He'd return to take in a brief pint and down the measure

indicators.note: to take in means to enclose, so one piece is placed inside the other
return signals that the letters of the word before are read backwards

parts.note: the contraction written without its apostrophe
PT is the short form of pint

explanation.surface: A man goes back to have a quick half and knock it back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses the contraction and 'to take in' encloses the short pint. 'down the measure' means the measurement taken downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Depth is the measurement taken downwards, from the surface to the bottom.

clue.text: Germany to float currency ? It's in the paper

definitions.meaning: the German mark set floating on the sea, read as a cryptic picture
a faint design pressed into paper during manufacture, visible against light

explanation.surface: A news item about Germany letting its currency float, printed in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a cryptic picture: the mark, Germany's old currency, floated on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Banknotes and fine stationery carry a translucent maker's design impressed in the sheet, so it is literally in the paper.

clue.text: Some agreement, but some of it is slight

indicators.note: some of it says only a part of the preceding words is taken, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: A partial accord, though part of it amounts to very little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of it' points back to 'Some agreement', where the letters run across the join of the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre describes something scanty or thin, the same as slight.

clue.text: After a good look, sell back the animals

parts.note: to gaze is to have a long, steady look

indicators.note: back tells us the word sell is written in reverse order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone eyes the goods carefully, then sells them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' is only surface: the look comes first in the answer, and 'back' reverses the verb that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazelles are small antelopes, a kind of animal.

clue.text: High-jinks ?

parts.note: jinks means dodging movements, done high up in the air by a stunt pilot

explanation.definitionFit: Aerobatics are stunt manoeuvres performed by aircraft, literally tricks high in the sky.

clue.text: Giant bird if old …

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
an was an old word for if, as in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A huge bird, if it is an ancient one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' meaning 'if' is archaic English ("an it please you").
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the Titans were a race of giants, so a titan is any giant figure.

clue.text: … puzzling giant mice

annotationWithheld.why: '... puzzling giant mice' as held: ENIGMATIC is an anagram of GIANT MICE, but 'puzzling' is the only word for both the definition and the anagram signal, a word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Strong Mohammedan, say ?

indicators.note: say signals that the word is to be spoken and heard

parts.note: a strong man, a muscleman

explanation.surface: A strong Muslim, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: Mussulman is an old word for a Muslim; it is pronounced like 'muscle man', a strong person.
explanation.definitionFit: Mussulman is an archaic term for a Muslim, an adherent of the faith of Muhammad.

clue.text: A difficult race with turns at St Moritz

definitions.text: A difficult race with turns at St Moritz

indicators.note: difficult suggests the letters are troublesome and need sorting out

explanation.surface: A tough race with sharp bends at a Swiss resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'difficult' rearranges RACE and TURNS. The whole clue also describes the famous ice toboggan run at the Swiss resort.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cresta Run is the steep, bending ice track for skeleton tobogganing at St Moritz.

clue.text: What I'd say 'Hard cheese " for ?

indicators.note: what I would say points to how the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: rock is something hard
the word for, spoken, matches the last syllable of the cheese, whose T is silent in French

explanation.surface: Someone asks what they would say 'hard luck' for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What I'd say' means pronounced: 'Hard' is ROCK, said like ROQUE, and 'for' sounds the final syllable because the French T is silent. 'Hard cheese' is British for bad luck.
explanation.definitionFit: Roquefort is a French blue sheep's-milk cheese.

clue.text: Lacking verbal originality when giving the price

definitions.meaning: repeating another's words rather than one's own

explanation.surface: A dealer stating a price in stock phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: Quoting means repeating someone else's words, and also naming an estimated cost.

clue.text: Form of European command

definitions.meaning: the outline or form of something
the Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, NATO's command centre

explanation.surface: A form issued by a European headquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAPE is the acronym of Supreme Headquarters Allied Powers Europe, NATO's military command.
explanation.definitionFit: A shape is an outline or configuration, and the NATO headquarters' initials spell the same word.

clue.text: Indirectly request airman to go around North

parts.note: to ask is to request

indicators.note: to go around means to encircle, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: an ace is a top fighter pilot

explanation.surface: A request that a pilot fly around the north, put obliquely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go around' wraps the pilot round the compass letter; 'Indirectly' fits askance in its sense of sideways, obliquely.
explanation.definitionFit: Askance means sideways or obliquely, hence indirectly.

clue.text: Coupé to set down the principal en route?

parts.note: to drop someone is to set them down from a vehicle
the head is the principal of a school

explanation.surface: A two-door car used to drop the headmaster off on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: A drophead coupé is a car with a folding roof, so 'Coupé' alone stands for the full name.
explanation.definitionFit: A drophead is a convertible coupé, a two-door car whose roof folds down.

clue.text: Lovebirds?

parts.note: in northern England 'love' and a certain waterfowl are both terms of endearment

explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is a British term of endearment, like 'love', so these are birds that are also loves.
explanation.definitionFit: These waterfowl share their name with the affectionate British address 'duck', making them loving birds.

clue.text: Is he any the worse for laughing ?

definitions.text: Is he any the worse for laughing ?

indicators.note: the worse for wear suggests the letters are damaged and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a man suffered from a fit of the giggles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the worse' rearranges HE ANY. The laughing hyena is known for its cackling call.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted hyena is called the laughing hyena for its cackling cry.

clue.text: The last thing to be kicked

definitions.text: The last thing to be kicked

parts.words: The last thing to be kicked
parts.note: from the idiom for dying, kicking a certain pail is the final act of a life

explanation.definitionFit: To kick the bucket means to die, so the pail is the final thing anyone kicks.

clue.text: Plant a singular 22 Dn

parts.note: one duck, in cricket a score of zero

explanation.surface: A plant called a lone duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 Down is DUCKS; one duck is a cricket score of nought, NIL. Anil is the indigo plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is a West Indian shrub from which indigo dye is made.

clue.text: Nicer, or it could be with some means of judging

indicators.note: could be suggests the letters might form something else if rearranged

explanation.surface: Something nicer, or it might come with a way of assessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be' asks for the letters of NICER OR IT in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A criterion is a standard by which things are judged.

clue.text: This key is not " the key of the door "

definitions.text: This key is not " the key of the door

parts.words: This key is not " the key of the door
parts.note: the key of the door is the traditional gift at twenty-one, coming of age; a musical key can be one not yet of age

explanation.walkthrough: 'The key of the door' is the British symbol of turning 21, the old age of majority.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor is someone under the age of majority who has not got the key of the door, and minor is also a musical key.

clue.text: Warnings given when jargon is the back-answer

indicators.note: back-answer tells us the words are answered backwards, read in reverse

parts.note: slang is informal jargon

explanation.surface: Warnings issued when someone answers back in jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the back-answer' reverses the two words together, as one run of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Signals are cautionary indications, such as railway warning lights.

clue.text: Light architectural feature

definitions.meaning: a portable lamp with a protective case
a small windowed turret crowning a dome or roof

explanation.surface: A light feature of a building's design.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern is a cased lamp, and in architecture a glazed turret on a dome that admits light.
